title: ChekOut: answer the question the shopper asked
text: The ChekOut agent answers the shopper's question first, and what retrieval finds decides the layout: words when no product fits, one card for one clear match, a bundle when products belong together. I re-set the panel from a canned support widget into a reading surface, with product names and prices in bold inside the sentence.

fills.alt: One clear match gets one product card

receipts.label: ChekOut AI case study

fills.caption: One clear match: one card, and why it fits.
fills.explain: A question with one clear answer in the catalog gets a single card and the reason for it, not a carousel. One intent, one product.

fills.alt: A bundle of products that belong together

receipts.label: ChekOut AI case study

fills.caption: Products that only work together arrive as one set.
fills.explain: When the shopper needs several items that belong together, retrieval returns them as a set and the panel shows them as one bundle. The shopper never asked for a bundle mode; the layout followed the answer.

fills.text: HOW: The shopper never picks a mode. The panel takes its shape from whatever retrieval returned, as the clips show.

title: ChekOut: motion that carries state
text: Every ChekOut animation tells the shopper what the agent is doing: a thinking state while it works, products arriving in a carousel, detail opening beside the thread, and a card that confirms an add in place. I shipped them in July 2026.

fills.alt: The thinking state, then the reply fades in

receipts.label: ChekOut AI case study

fills.caption: The thinking state holds the shopper's place, then the reply fades in.
fills.explain: A static panel can't show that the agent is working. The thinking state holds the spot where the answer will land, then the newest reply fades in word by word.

fills.alt: Products arrive with the answer in a carousel

receipts.label: ChekOut AI case study

fills.caption: Products arrive with the answer, and the thread stays on screen.
fills.explain: Products come in with the reply as a carousel, so the shopper can browse without losing the conversation above it.

fills.alt: The closed launcher offers two suggested questions on hover

receipts.label: Agent platform case study

fills.caption: Hovering the closed launcher offers two suggested questions.
fills.explain: Before the chat is even open, hovering the launcher on a merchant's store offers two suggested questions, so a shopper who doesn't know what to ask has a place to start. Merchants can turn them off in the builder.

title: Christine Valmy: three fixes, three sessions
text: Three Christine Valmy test sessions each found one thing students tripped on, and I fixed it before the next: dropdowns read as topics, social links sat in the wrong place, and the agent spoke only English when many applicants spoke Spanish first. The agent and every label now work in both languages, and the widget was audited to WCAG AA.

receipts.label: Christine Valmy case study

fills.caption: After: one message box; the agent picks location and course from the text.

title: Christine Valmy: agent architecture
text: A React widget in a WordPress plugin sends each message to an n8n workflow on Google Cloud in front of the agent, which answers through RAG from the school's documents. Routing runs through MCP: Claude answers in English, Gemini in Spanish. Finished chats become leads in priority buckets, conversation and lead data land in BigQuery, and the inquiry form writes to the school's Creatio CRM.

fills.alt: Christine Valmy agent architecture: students use the widget on the school's WordPress site; each message goes to n8n on Google Cloud, which reaches the agent (RAG, routed through MCP: Claude for English, Gemini for Spanish); finished chats become leads for officers; conversation and lead data land in BigQuery; the inquiry form creates a lead in the school's Creatio CRM
fills.caption: From a student's question to a sorted lead.
fills.explain: Follow a student's message: the widget sends it to n8n on Google Cloud, n8n reaches the agent, and the reply comes back with the conversation stage. The agent answers from the school's documents through RAG, Claude in English and Gemini in Spanish, routed through MCP. Finished chats become leads, the data lands in BigQuery, and the inquiry form goes to the school's CRM.

title: How did he open it to other people safely
text: Before letting other job seekers sign in in October 2026, I scoped every route to an access tier, rate-limited everything that spends tokens, and made the tests unable to touch real data.

fills.text: THE PROBLEM: By May a second person was using it, but the agents run on my machine, spend real model credits, and keep everyone's search beside mine. Letting more people in could not expose anyone's data or run up the bill.
